CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his overall condition since the last visit. He states that his adherence to the prescribed sertraline at 200 mg daily continues, and he has maintained his usage of trazodone at 50 mg nightly, which he believes has contributed to a marginal increase in sleep duration, now averaging 6 hours per night. However, he still experiences difficulty with sleep initiation and frequent nocturnal awakenings, resulting in a feeling of non-restorative sleep.
Mr. Smith reports that his fatigue persists, particularly during the workweek, attributing it to both his sleep disturbances and ongoing project deadlines. He notes that his headache frequency has remained consistent, with episodes occurring four times weekly, although he describes a slight decrease in intensity, now rated as 6/10. He continues to take amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly and ibuprofen as needed, but reports that he is still experiencing some resistance to over-the-counter analgesics. Mr. Smith has continued his acupuncture sessions twice a week, which he feels have provided partial relief.
He remains engaged in his yoga practice and mindfulness techniques, although he admits that work-related stressors continue to be a significant challenge. He has been utilizing relaxation techniques more consistently, which has been beneficial for managing his anxiety levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 6. Amitriptyline 20 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that project deadlines remain a source of stress. He has maintained his commitment to physical activity, attending yoga classes regularly and incorporating meditation practices into his routine. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he occasionally indulges in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent difficulty initiating sleep; anxiety manageable with therapy and medication; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency and intensity; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Notable fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce the tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Schedule follow-up therapy sessions to continue enhancing coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg; consider increasing dosage if sleep quality does not improve further. Continue melatonin at 10 mg; maintain CBT-I strategies and closely monitor sleep patterns. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Due to the persistent nature of the headaches, increase amitriptyline to 30 mg nightly. Assess the impact of acupuncture and discuss the potential for preventive medication such as topiramate if headaches do not improve with the dosage adjustment. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Emphasize the importance of maintaining physical activity and mindfulness practices. Consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization. Explore sleep hygiene techniques to further improve sleep quality.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-01-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
